lawyer: M Nurullah with M Shafiullah, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner
parties:
Al-Haj Akhtaruzzaman Chowdhury (Babu) ------ Petitioner
vs
Mohammad Kabir & others ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Anwarul Hoque J: This is an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and is directed against an order dated 14.11.93 passed by Judge in charge, 1st. Additional District and Sessions Judge, Chittagong in Election Tribunal Case No. 3 of 1991. 

 2. It is the case of the petitioner that he is a sitting member of Parliament duly elected in last General Election held on 27.2.91. The opposite party No. 1 as petitioner, instituted an election case being Election Tribunal Case No. 3 of 1991 before the Election Commissioner, Sher-e-Banglanagar, Dhaka which was referred to the learned District Judge, Chittagong for trial in his capacity as the Election Tribunal for Chittagong District. In that election petition relief was sought in the form of a declaration to declare that the election of the present petitioner as member of Parliament from Constituency No. 290 Chittagong 12 (Anwara-West Patiya) is invalid, illegal and also for a further declaration that the petitioner should be declared as member of the parliament on the allegations that the petitioner adopted illegal means and corrupt practices and spent huge amounts by constructing several gates, election officers using number of transports to carry the voters to the polling stations and also influenced the opposite party No. 12, the Assistant Returning Officer. It is also the case that he hired anti-social and armed miscreants who being armed with cocktails firearms created terror and coerced the voters to vote for him in different polling stations mentioned in the election petition. It is also the allegation that the re-election held in seven centres were also vitiated due to illegal activities of the present petitioner and in the premises he prayed for the declaration as mentioned above. 

 5. On transfer of the learned Judge Mr. Md. Ismail Mia to First Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, the case was being taken up by the judge-in-charge of that court acting also as judge-in-charge, relating to Election Tribunal Md. Syed Enayetullah who in spite of petitioner's prayer to adjourn the hearing till the Election Commission legally appoints a judge as Election Tribunal to dispose of election petitions including the election petition in which the petitioner is the opposite party No. 1, the judge in-charge rejected the contention of the petitioner by an order dated 17.10.93 and proceeded with the hearing of the election case filed against the petitioner by examining the witnesses of the opposite Party No. 1. Thereafter the opposite party No. 1 namely, the election petitioner on 14.11.93 after intimating the court that he had concluded the examination of his witnesses prayed for personal appearance of the petitioner under Article 56 of the Representation of the People Order, 1972 and pursuant to that the learned judge in-charge directed the petitioner to appear in person by 17.11.93. The present petitioner namely, Alhaj Aktaruzzaman Chowdhury (Babu) filed an application to examine the witnesses on his behalf and also prayed for the examination of the petitioner's duly constituted attorney and other witnesses. The learned Judge agreed only to examine the petitioner's constituted attorney and then to strike off the defence and to give an ex parte decision on petitioner's failure for personal appearance. The court adjourned the case to 4.1.94 after examining the attorney of the petitioner as PW fixing the next date on 9.1.94 keeping the matter of personal appearance of the petitioner open. After conclusion of the evidence of DW 1 expressing reluctance to examine further witnesses on behalf of the petitioner unless the petitioner appears in person and gives evidence in the election case, he passed the order which is challenged before this court. 

 6. It is the contention of the learned Advocate Mr. M. Nurullah that the Tribunal committed error of law in ordering personal appearance of the petitioner keeping in view the real purport of Article 56 of the Representation of People Order, 1972 without any legal consideration to the conditions to be adhered to for personal appearance as contemplated. Order 3 rule 1, Order 5 rule 3 and Order 10 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure which as procedure matter have been made applicable in case of trial of election petitions and, as such, there is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. It is the further case of the learned Advocate that the judge in charge now dealing with the Election Case No. 3 of 1991 having no locus standi and jurisdiction in respect of hearing of the election case as a persona designata, the matter having assigned to the District Judge only, the order passed has occasioned a failure of justice making the impugned order as wholly illegal and unsustainable in law. Since the learned Judge in charge has allowed the petitioner to represent him in the case through his constituted attorney, the impugned order concerning personal appearance of the petitioner is contradictory and is the result of non application of judicial mind and the same having occasioned failure of justice, the impugned order is bad in law as well as in fact. 

 9. It is the case of the petitioner before this court that the Notification having appointed District and Sessions Judge of each Sessions Division of different areas to be the Election Commission, only the said person could constitute the Tribunal and the said power and function cannot be delegated by the District and Sessions Judge to Additional District Judge, as was done in the instant case and therefore the continuation of the trial of the instant petition case before a Judge-in-charge of the District and Sessions Judge and Additional District Judge and Sessions Judge is illegal, without jurisdiction. It is an exercise of power by usurpation of jurisdiction and therefore a nullity. 

 10. We have already referred to the various provisions of the law which are relevant in order to examine the contention of the petitioner. It has been provided in sub-article 2 of Article 53 that a tribunal shall consist of a person who is or has been or is as the time of his retirement as a District and Sessions Judge was qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court. It has not totally prohibited the Additional District Judge or Judge-in-charge for acting as Tribunal. When the Notification of the Commission refers to the District Judges and Sessions Judge to be Election Tribunal it need be read along with Article 152(1) of the Constitution in the definition clause which defines District Judges to include an Additional District Judge. This is the Constitutional definition of the expression of District Judge and need be so understood as to include an Additional District Judge and a Judge-in-charge of that court of Additional or District Judge. Therefore, an exercise of power of an Election Tribunal by an Additional District Judge and or Judge-in-charge of that court or District Judge is. not an usurpation of jurisdiction. It can be tried by the District Judge or by an Additional District Judge, or by a Judge-in-charge of those courts when so required. We further find that this jurisdictional point has not been taken in the instant case specifically. The earlier petition challenging jurisdiction has been long rejected and accepted by the parties as such, as the matter has proceeded in the Additional District Judge Court acting as Tribunal who has ordered for the personal appearance of the present petitioner when only the petitioner rushed to this court. In the instant case we find that there is no absence of jurisdiction of the Tribunal. 

 11. Coming back to the order of personal appearance which is the impugned order in the instant case, it is seen that the Representation of People Order clearly provided that the Tribunal, if it thinks fit, may order personal appearance of the party before the court and it is in the proviso to Article 56 which provided that the Tribunal may, where it considers necessary, direct any party to appear in person. This order therefore can be passed by the Tribunal if it considers it necessary to do so. This question of necessity therefore need be a consideration to be considered objectively before passing such an order. When we look at the order we find that there is no absence of such objective consideration of the necessity for personal appearance. The Tribunal while ordering personal appearance had referred to the provision of Article 56 of the Order and proceeded to find that as there are personal allegation of corrupt and illegal practice alleged to have been committed by Alhaj Aktaruzaman Chowdhury, the Court considers that as there are witnesses to depose against him and in order to controvert those it needs his personal attendance and it is so necessary for ends of justice. Considering so the Tribunal directed the petitioner Alhaj Aktaruzzaman Chowdhury to appear in person and depose in Court on 17.11.93. That date is however over because we are now in January, 1994. The personal appearance before that Court on that day and even today had not been complied with. If Alhaj Aktaruzzaman Chowdhury has personal inconvenience to be present on that or any other future day he may make a prayer before the court for time after going to the court on subsequent day but the order need be complied with. The time may be allowed if he can prove to the satisfaction of the court that he is unable to move. This however is between Aktaruzzaman Chowdhury and the court to which we do not want to make any comment but so far this petition is concerned we find no substance, which is summarily rejected.
